claims.text: The base alloy has composition Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 in atomic percent.
The base alloy forms several primary non-eutectic crystalline phases during thermal processing.
The base alloy exhibits a complex, multistep crystallization sequence.
The proposed intervention is to add approximately 2 at.% B to the base alloy.
Boron is a nucleation-inhibiting alloying element in this alloy system.
A cooling rate greater than approximately 10^5 K/s represents a critical-rate regime for glass formation in the base or B-modified alloy.
Added B atoms will introduce atomic-size mismatch and alter chemical bonding.
The B-induced size mismatch and bonding changes will disrupt local atomic ordering.
Disruption of local atomic ordering by B will reduce the probability of crystalline-phase nucleation and growth.
B addition will increase the kinetic barrier for crystallization.
B addition will reduce atomic mobility during cooling.
The increased crystallization barrier and reduced mobility will delay or suppress initial crystallization events during cooling.
Delayed nucleation kinetics will retain the amorphous phase over a longer temperature interval during reheating.
Under identical cooling rates, the B-modified alloy will retain a larger amorphous volume fraction than the base alloy.
The B-modified alloy will exhibit a delayed or simplified multistep crystallization sequence during reheating.
B addition will improve the thermal stability of the retained amorphous phase.
The unmodified alloy undergoes extensive primary crystallization during both rapid and slower cooling.

contradictions.description: The stated reheating boundary requires reheating to remain below the baseline crystallization-onset temperature, where crystallization peaks or a multistep crystallization sequence should not occur, but the predicted outcome and experiment require observing and comparing crystallization onset and sequence during staged reheating.
